title: Market Basket — Groceries
description: Association rule mining on grocery baskets with support/confidence/lift.
overview_content:
Lab intro

Scenario: A supermarket chain has scanned 9,835 checkout baskets and wants to know which products are bought together. The answers drive real business decisions: which items to place on adjacent shelves, which products to bundle in promotions, and what to recommend at the checkout. You will implement association-rule mining (the Apriori idea) in pure Python — no mlxtend — to discover these patterns. You will learn: parsing headerless variable-length transaction data, transaction encoding, the three rule metrics (support, confidence, lift), Apriori-style candidate generation, and how to filter rules for actionable insights. Time: ~60 minutes. Level: Intermediate. Needs: pandas + matplotlib. Env: 🟢 Colab only.
steps_content:
Exercises (do these!)

Exercise 1 — Top 10 Itemsets by Support

Compute the support of every 1-itemset and every 2-itemset. Report the top 10 1-itemsets and the top 10 2-itemsets by support. Expected: top 1-itemset = whole milk (0.2555); top 2-itemset = {other vegetables, whole milk} (0.0748).

Follow-up: How many frequent 2-itemsets survive a 1% support threshold? Check: 213.

Exercise 2 — Rules for "Whole Milk" Consequent

Generate all rules where the consequent is whole milk (min support 0.01, min confidence 0.10). Report the count and the top rule by confidence. Expected: 45 rules; top = butter → whole milk (conf ≈ 0.4972, lift ≈ 1.9461).

Follow-up: What is the confidence of root vegetables → whole milk? Check: ≈ 0.4487.

Exercise 3 — High-Lift Rules Only

Filter all 2-itemset rules to those with lift > 2. Report the count and the top rule by lift. Expected: 44 rules; top = root vegetables → beef (lift ≈ 3.0404).

Follow-up: What is the lift of tropical fruit → pip fruit? Check: ≈ 2.5746.

Hint

For Exercise 3, iterate over freq_2, and for each itemset {a, b} generate both directions: a → b and b → a. Compute lift as conf / (item_counts[b] / N) and keep rules where lift > 2.
